name: Classic Route
approach: Start at the Snow Lake Trailhead on Stevens Canyon Road (~1.5 miles east of Reflection Lakes, elev. ~4,500 ft). Follow the maintained Snow Lake Trail about 1 mile, with roughly 350 ft of up-and-down, to Snow Lake at ~4,600 ft — the last reliable water source. Skirt the west/north shore of the lake; the maintained tread continues a short way (about 1.2 miles from the TH) over a tree-covered rise before petering out into talus. From there work up and right toward an obvious talus/dirt gully on the peak's NW side — a climbers' path picks up again on a heather bench near the top of the gully. Follow this into the basin below Unicorn Peak, ascending moraine along the left (south) side of the small permanent snow patch/glacier remnant in the basin (crampons/an axe are handy in early season on the couloir above, though not strictly required most of the year). A climbers' path traverses below the cliffs here, offering easier travel than the loose scree and talus on either side, and leads up to the saddle (Unicorn Col) just west of the summit. From the saddle, a use trail traverses east/around the south side of the main summit block, across a final loose scree slope, to the base of the summit horn. Total approach is roughly 2.5-3 miles one-way with about 2,400 ft of gain; expect route-finding through talus and some loose rock once off the maintained trail, and possible steep snow in the gully/basin into mid-summer.

approach_variants.name: Snow Lake and Unicorn Col to the middle line on the summit horn
approach_variants.notes:
Shared approach with the peak's other summit-block lines: from the Snow Lake trailhead, take the maintained Snow Lake Trail about a mile and roughly 350 ft of up-and-down to Snow Lake, the last water. Skirt the west and north shore; the tread continues a short way over a tree-covered rise before petering out into talus.

Work up and right toward the obvious talus and dirt gully on the peak's northwest side; a climbers' path picks up again on a heather bench near the top of the gully. Follow it into the basin, then climb moraine along the left side of the small permanent snow patch to Unicorn Col just west of the summit. A climbers' path traverses below the cliffs — easier travel than the scree either side — and leads east around the south side to the base of the summit horn.

The climb itself is a single pitch of blocky low-fifth-class climbing, about 40-50 ft, on the south and southeast face, with one fixed piton mid-pitch.

Roughly 2.5-3 miles one-way and about 2,400 ft of gain.
hazards: Loose blocks on the approach scramble to the base of the horn
A short exposed pitch above broken ground where a fall has real consequence
A rappel that may not reach the ground on a 30 m rope, particularly with an open moat late season
An old bleached snag at the top that is no longer a sound anchor
Two different rappel lines off the same block landing in different places
approach_variants.baseFinding:
Left to right along the foot of the horn: the roof, the classic route, Open Book. All three start within about 70 ft of each other and all three finish at the same slung block, so the bottom is the only place this can be got right.

The classic route is the middle one, and it takes the south and southeast face direct — blocky low-fifth climbing straight up, one pitch of about 40-50 ft, with one fixed piton mid-pitch. A piton at half height on open face is the positive confirmation.

The distance test is the practical one and it works by feel rather than by sight:
  — The roof starts about 20 ft to your left, at the point where the ridgeline meets the block.
  — Open Book starts about 50 ft to your right, at two wide, left-leaning cracks.

So the two negatives are tactile, which is what you want when the horn is in cloud: if you are fighting a wide awkward crack that wants big cams, you have walked past this route to the right and you are on Open Book. If there is a roof over your head and you are in a gully or chimney, you have gone left past it and you are on the roof, at 5.6.

Character test: this is blocky face and crack climbing on the open face. Not inside a chimney, not in a wide crack. If you are inside anything, you are on a neighbour.

Why it matters: this is the middle grade of the three — 5.4, against Open Book's easy fifth and The Roof's 5.6. Being one line out changes the grade in whichever direction you drifted, on a short pitch above broken ground.

Descent detail worth settling at the top rather than over the edge: there are effectively two rappel lines off the summit block, one dropping to the notch and the ground below the horn, the other landing on the snow patch side. A 30 m rope has been reported as just short depending on which one you use and on how open the moat is late season; 40 m removes the guesswork. Use the rock horn — the old bleached snag some older reports mention is no longer sound.

itinerary.cal: Best in late spring/early summer when the approach bowl still holds consolidated snow; by late summer it's loose scree, and Stevens Canyon Rd only opens once cleared of winter snow (typically late May-June).

days.note: The Classic Route is the most popular of Unicorn's three summit-block lines (a single ~40-50 ft pitch of 5.4 rock/low-5th climbing). Parties hike past Snow Lake, climb a steep snow/scree bowl to the west col, traverse across a moat onto rock, then lead or solo the short pitch to the summit and rappel the same line.
days.title: Car-to-car: Snow Lake approach, Classic Route, rappel descent

schedule.label: Leave Snow Lake trailhead
schedule.detail: Stevens Canyon Rd, ~1.5 mi east of Reflection Lakes.

schedule.label: Top out the west col/saddle
schedule.detail: Steep snow gully or scree bowl; best with consolidated snow.

schedule.label: Base of the summit block
schedule.detail: Traverse east across a moat/gap onto rock below the south face.

schedule.label: Summit via Classic Route (5.4)
schedule.detail: Single pitch, natural gear; rope up for the exposure even though it's short.

schedule.label: Rappel and hike back to trailhead
schedule.detail: Natural summit anchors, then reverse the col, bowl, and lakeshore trail.

days.objective: Climb the Classic Route (5.4) to Unicorn Peak's summit pinnacle

itinerary.totalNote: A single long day: roughly 8 hrs car-to-car, ~2,600 ft gain and 5.5 mi round trip, with one short 5.4 pitch at the top.
